requirements.quote:
In any case, the model used in this memo assumes that the resolver is
multiplexing attention between multiple requests, some from the client,
and some internally generated.  Each request is represented by some
state information,
requirements.condition: For the resolver request-processing model described in this memo.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent each request with state information.
requirements.why_checkable: Concurrent client and internally generated requests can be inspected for individual request state.

requirements.quote:
The key algorithm uses the state
information of the request to select the next name server address to
query, and also computes a timeout which will cause the next action
should a response not arrive.
requirements.condition: When choosing the next name server address for a request.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the request state information to select the next name server address to query.
requirements.why_checkable: Server-selection code and successive selections can be checked against the request state.

requirements.quote:
The key algorithm uses the state
information of the request to select the next name server address to
query, and also computes a timeout which will cause the next action
should a response not arrive.
requirements.condition: When sending a query for a request.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute a timeout that causes the next action if no response arrives.
requirements.why_checkable: A suppressed response can demonstrate whether the computed timeout triggers further request processing.

requirements.quote:
The key algorithm uses the state
information of the request to select the next name server address to
query, and also computes a timeout which will cause the next action
should a response not arrive.  The next action will usually be a
transmission to some other server, but may be a temporary error to the

client.
requirements.condition: When a query receives no response and its timeout causes the next action.
requirements.error_behavior: May return a temporary error to the client as the next action.
requirements.why_checkable: The no-response timeout branch can be checked for this permitted temporary-error outcome without requiring it.

requirements.quote: The resolver always starts with a list of server names to query (SLIST).
requirements.condition: At the start of a resolver search.
requirements.required_behavior: Start with a list of server names to query, called SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: Search initialization can be inspected for the server-name list.

requirements.quote:
The resolver always starts with a list of server names to query (SLIST).
This list will be all NS RRs which correspond to the nearest ancestor
zone that the resolver knows about.
requirements.condition: When initializing SLIST from known NS records.
requirements.required_behavior: Populate the initial server-name list with all NS RRs corresponding to the nearest ancestor zone known to the resolver.
requirements.why_checkable: Given cached NS records at multiple ancestor zones, the initial SLIST can be compared with the complete NS set at the nearest known ancestor.

requirements.quote:
To avoid startup problems, the
resolver should have a set of default servers which it will ask should
it have no current NS RRs which are appropriate.
requirements.condition: To support startup when no appropriate current NS RRs are available.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should have a set of default servers.
requirements.why_checkable: Resolver configuration and initialization can be checked for the recommended default-server set.

requirements.quote:
To avoid startup problems, the
resolver should have a set of default servers which it will ask should
it have no current NS RRs which are appropriate.
requirements.condition: When no appropriate current NS RRs are available and the recommended default-server set is present.
requirements.required_behavior: Ask the default servers.
requirements.why_checkable: An empty or unsuitable NS cache can demonstrate whether query selection uses the configured default servers.

requirements.quote:
The resolver then adds
to SLIST all of the known addresses for the name servers, and may start
parallel requests to acquire the addresses of the servers when the
resolver has the name, but no addresses, for the name servers.
requirements.condition: When adding addresses for the name servers in SLIST.
requirements.required_behavior: Add all known addresses for those name servers to SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: Known multiple addresses for a listed server can be compared with the initialized address entries.

requirements.quote:
The resolver then adds
to SLIST all of the known addresses for the name servers, and may start
parallel requests to acquire the addresses of the servers when the
resolver has the name, but no addresses, for the name servers.
requirements.condition: When the resolver knows a name server name but has no addresses for that name server.
requirements.required_behavior: May start parallel requests to acquire the name server addresses.
requirements.why_checkable: The missing-address branch can be inspected for permitted parallel address-resolution requests without requiring parallelism.

requirements.quote:
To complete initialization of SLIST, the resolver attaches whatever
history information it has to the each address in SLIST.
requirements.condition: When completing initialization of SLIST.
requirements.required_behavior: Attach whatever history information is available to each address in SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: Initialized address entries can be compared with the available history records.

requirements.quote:
To complete initialization of SLIST, the resolver attaches whatever
history information it has to the each address in SLIST.  This will
usually consist of some sort of weighted averages for the response time
of the address, and the batting average of the address (i.e., how often
the address responded at all to the request).  Note that this
information should be kept on a per address basis, rather than on a per
name server basis, because the response time and batting average of a
particular server may vary considerably from address to address.
requirements.condition: When storing name server response-time and response-success history.
requirements.required_behavior: History information should be kept separately for each server address rather than aggregated only by name server.
requirements.why_checkable: A server with multiple addresses and different response histories can reveal the history lookup and update keys.

requirements.quote:
Note
also that this information is actually specific to a resolver address /
server address pair, so a resolver with multiple addresses may wish to
keep separate histories for each of its addresses.
requirements.condition: When a resolver has multiple addresses and keeps server-response history.
requirements.required_behavior: May keep separate histories for each resolver address, keyed by the resolver-address and server-address pair.
requirements.why_checkable: History keys can be inspected for this optional separation by the local address used.

requirements.quote:
To complete initialization of SLIST, the resolver attaches whatever
history information it has to the each address in SLIST.  This will
usually consist of some sort of weighted averages for the response time
of the address, and the batting average of the address (i.e., how often
the address responded at all to the request).  Note that this
information should be kept on a per address basis, rather than on a per
name server basis, because the response time and batting average of a
particular server may vary considerably from address to address.  Note
also that this information is actually specific to a resolver address /
server address pair, so a resolver with multiple addresses may wish to
keep separate histories for each of its addresses.  Part of this step
must deal with addresses which have no such history; in this case an
expected round trip time of 5-10 seconds should be the worst case, with
lower estimates for the same local network, etc.
requirements.condition: When completing SLIST initialization for an address with no history.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle the address even though no history information is available.
requirements.why_checkable: The text requires dealing with missing history but does not specify a concrete handling behavior beyond the separately extracted round-trip-time recommendations.

requirements.quote:
Part of this step
must deal with addresses which have no such history; in this case an
expected round trip time of 5-10 seconds should be the worst case, with
lower estimates for the same local network, etc.
requirements.condition: When initializing the expected round-trip time for an address that has no history.
requirements.required_behavior: An expected round-trip time of 5-10 seconds should be used as the worst case.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial estimate for an unknown remote address can be checked against the recommended worst-case range.

requirements.quote:
Part of this step
must deal with addresses which have no such history; in this case an
expected round trip time of 5-10 seconds should be the worst case, with
lower estimates for the same local network, etc.
requirements.condition: When initializing the expected round-trip time for an address on the same local network that has no history.
requirements.required_behavior: The expected round-trip-time estimate should be lower than the recommended 5-10-second worst-case estimate.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial estimates for local and worst-case remote addresses can be compared; this is the local-network part of the stated recommendation.

requirements.quote:
Note that whenever a delegation is followed, the resolver algorithm
reinitializes SLIST.
requirements.condition: Whenever the resolver follows a delegation.
requirements.required_behavior: Reinitialize SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: A delegation response can be used to check that the subsequent server list is rebuilt.

requirements.quote:
The information establishes a partial ranking of the available name
server addresses.  Each time an address is chosen and the state should
be altered to prevent its selection again until all other addresses have
been tried.
requirements.condition: Each time a name server address is chosen.
requirements.required_behavior: The state should be altered to prevent choosing that address again until all other available addresses have been tried.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of selections from multiple available addresses can be checked for premature repetition.

requirements.quote:
The timeout for each transmission should be 50-100% greater
than the average predicted value to allow for variance in response.
requirements.condition: For each query transmission.
requirements.required_behavior: The timeout should be 50-100 percent greater than the average predicted response time.
requirements.why_checkable: The computed timeout can be compared with 1.5 to 2 times the average predicted value.

requirements.quote:
- The resolver may encounter a situation where no addresses are
     available for any of the name servers named in SLIST, and
     where the servers in the list are precisely those which would
     normally be used to look up their own addresses.  This
     situation typically occurs when the glue address RRs have a
     smaller TTL than the NS RRs marking delegation, or when the
     resolver caches the result of a NS search.  The resolver
     should detect this condition and restart the search at the
     next ancestor zone, or alternatively at the root.
requirements.condition: When no addresses are available for any server named in SLIST and those same servers would normally resolve their own addresses.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should detect this circular missing-address condition.
requirements.why_checkable: A delegation whose NS records remain cached after all required address records are unavailable can exercise condition detection.

requirements.quote:
- The resolver may encounter a situation where no addresses are
     available for any of the name servers named in SLIST, and
     where the servers in the list are precisely those which would
     normally be used to look up their own addresses.  This
     situation typically occurs when the glue address RRs have a
     smaller TTL than the NS RRs marking delegation, or when the
     resolver caches the result of a NS search.  The resolver
     should detect this condition and restart the search at the

requirements.condition: When no addresses are available for any server named in SLIST and those same servers would normally resolve their own addresses.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should restart the search at the next ancestor zone or at the root.
requirements.why_checkable: After constructing the circular missing-address condition, subsequent queries can be checked for an ancestor-zone or root restart.

requirements.quote:
- If a resolver gets a server error or other bizarre response
     from a name server, it should remove it from SLIST, and may
     wish to schedule an immediate transmission to the next
     candidate server address.
requirements.condition: When a resolver receives a server error from a name server.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should remove that name server from SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: A server-error response can be injected and subsequent SLIST entries inspected.

requirements.quote:
- If a resolver gets a server error or other bizarre response
     from a name server, it should remove it from SLIST, and may
     wish to schedule an immediate transmission to the next
     candidate server address.
requirements.condition: When a resolver receives a server error from a name server.
requirements.required_behavior: May schedule an immediate transmission to the next candidate server address.
requirements.why_checkable: The server-error branch can be checked for this optional immediate failover without requiring it.

requirements.quote:
- If a resolver gets a server error or other bizarre response
     from a name server, it should remove it from SLIST, and may
     wish to schedule an immediate transmission to the next
     candidate server address.
requirements.condition: When a resolver receives another bizarre response from a name server.
requirements.required_behavior: The resolver should remove that name server from SLIST.
requirements.why_checkable: Removal is observable, but this chunk does not define which responses qualify as bizarre, so the triggering input class is unclear.

requirements.quote:
- If a resolver gets a server error or other bizarre response
     from a name server, it should remove it from SLIST, and may

requirements.condition: When a resolver receives another bizarre response from a name server.

requirements.why_checkable: An immediate next-server transmission is observable, but this chunk does not define which responses qualify as bizarre.
